bullets.text: A dam safety emergency began at Halvern Dam on the Sorrel River near Brindlemark in the Assek Valley on 9 September 2025, when the dam and its right abutment were reported damaged.

The alert level was raised from Yellow to Orange the following morning and a mandatory evacuation was ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow, with roughly 11,800 residents moved from the town and the figure later given as 12,400.
No casualties were reported in the window; the human impact consisted of large-scale evacuation and displacement from Brindlemark, Ferris Hollow and Quennard.

The Sorrel Basin Water Authority issued information on the dam, Brindlemark Police deployed to the town and assistance was provided to displaced people in Quennard, with the cause of the damage not yet stated.
Halvern Dam and its right abutment are reported damaged on the afternoon of the first day.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority issues information on the dam within the hour.
The next morning the alert level is raised from Yellow to Orange and a mandatory evacuation is ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow; roughly 11,800 residents leave the town.
By the evening of the second day the evacuee figure is given as 12,400, people are displaced from Quennard and assistance is provided there.
Brindlemark Police deploy to Brindlemark at the end of the window.
Halvern Dam and its right abutment were damaged.
A mandatory evacuation was ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow when the alert level was raised to Orange.
Roughly 11,800 residents were moved out of Brindlemark under the mandatory evacuation, and people were also evacuated from Ferris Hollow.
The number of people evacuated from Brindlemark rose to 12,400 by the evening of the second day.
People were displaced from Quennard as the evacuation widened beyond Brindlemark.
Brindlemark Police deployed to Brindlemark during the evacuation.
The alert level was raised from Yellow to Orange after the damage to Halvern Dam.
The Sorrel Basin Water Authority provided information on the condition of Halvern Dam.
Assistance was provided to displaced people in Quennard.
